# Agent A: accepted boundary recovery with durable shared storage

Status: initial independent discovery complete, 2026-10-07. Candidate and tests are proposed, not implemented or deployment qualified. No live execution, install, image operation, credential inspection, external contact, commit or push occurred. No canonical document or ticket was changed.

## Recommendation and strongest objection

The smallest credible extension restores application state on a fresh qualified sandbox rather than restoring VM memory. Keep the existing SDK runner, controller, supervisor, observation probe and exact original pending recovery adapter. Store opaque session entries in a transactional shared store with conditional append; use a separately durable POSIX workspace volume, retaining protected claims outside effect writable storage. Temporal commits only bounded accepted checkpoint references and decisions. Require authoritative termination of the prior execution before launching its replacement. If termination or state consistency is unresolved, park.

This is viable for recovery from verified stopped process/container/guest/host execution. It is not a recipe for automatic failover from every network partition: a lease expiring, Activity timing out or database ownership changing cannot stop an old process sending an external request. General arbitrary Bash safe automatic takeover during a partition remains unsupported unless the deployment proves effective termination or enforcement at every external capability. The strongest objection is availability: safe refusal can leave runs parked through a long control plane outage. If the product requires uninterrupted arbitrary effects through partitions, this candidate does not meet it; changing storage alone will not repair that requirement.

The application is greenfield per operator clarification. Existing integration library and fixtures are brownfield reference/dependency constraints, not a deployed application topology. No application source map exists or is claimed.

## Source baseline and retained evidence

Read repository AGENTS.md and Git status first. HEAD is c79bdb516f4a4fe343bb97c1c97b39f0d796c450, with the existing dirty implementation/docs/tests preserved. Read canonical-documents.md starting at Phase 1 independent verification checkpoint (2026-10-07), canonical specification/plan/work items and relevant evidence, private README/status map/Phase 0/Phase 1 and verification-20261007.md. Current checkpoints supersede historical IN PROGRESS paragraphs. Completed tickets remain DONE; DSR-0.6 and DSR-0.11 remain decisions, and no acceptance advances through discovery.

Reuse the recorded selected SDK 0.2.162 / CLI 2.1.274 original pending recovery proof and precise negative controls. Reuse final verification 752 passed/52 skipped selected, 747/54 minimum and 298 focused. These are Linux/Python 3.13 evidence, not distributed host failover or storage tests. Minimum SDK 0.2.153 / CLI 2.1.273 original recovery remains unsupported under the approved recorded failure disposition. Preserve synthetic resume DEFECT, original question runtime FAILs, actual billing uncertainty and consumed null accounting. Source hashes are in evidence.json. Do not reuse historical source bound live commands after fixture changes.

Material inspected source: _runner.py requires append_if_unchanged for original pending recovery, reads checkpoint from store, and guards head changes. _session_store.py FileSessionStore advertises single machine/local use: threading.Lock is process local; writes use O_APPEND, do not fsync, and no conditional append method exists. Mounting that store on a network volume does not supply the required recovery or distributed concurrency contract. ProofStore in write_recovery.py uses SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE and synchronous=FULL, explicitly on one host. HostSession is also explicitly local, not a distributed lease. These are bounded references; do not place SQLite files on a shared network mount as the production solution.

## Prior art and maturity inventory

Search used Temporal Docs connector (Activity heartbeat/cancellation/failure mechanisms), Atlas query wrapper, current official SDK/session storage docs, Linux open semantics, AWS EFS, Kubernetes PV and PostgreSQL documentation. Atlas combined keyword/semantic query did not supply a matching complete shared storage execution implementation. No absent search result is evidence that none exists. Public source examples and supplied documentation are references, not executed proof. No public discussion contact occurred. Exact new deployment versions remain unselected; pinned SDK/CLI are the qualified project lane, not registry latest.

| Component | Evidence and disposition | Maturity/version boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing runner and original pending adapter | Reuse; exact call/result route and refused unsupported child behavior | Current dirty source over published HEAD, selected SDK 0.2.162 / CLI 2.1.274 |
| Temporal Workflow, ordinary Activities, Updates and history | Reuse; ordinary persistence and retry primitives, external execution remains application responsibility | Existing proof server 1.32.0; application deployment version unselected |
| Anthropic SessionStore API/examples | Reference; opaque ordered UUID dedup entries, not sufficient distributed ownership | Current rolling docs queried 2026-10-07; pinned wheel behavior must be qualified |
| PostgreSQL | Candidate reference for transactionally conditional transcript append and receipts | Official current docs resolved PostgreSQL 18; patch/service/replication deployment unselected |
| AWS EFS Regional | Candidate reference for durable POSIX workspace | Current managed service docs, NFS client/kernel/mount options unselected; no local account assumed |
| Kubernetes PV/CSI | Optional deployment plumbing, not a correctness proof | Rolling docs, cluster/driver versions unselected |
| Worker specific queues | Reject as distributed durability mechanism; reference for locality only | Routing work to one host does not recover that host's lost disk |
| VM memory snapshot | Reject as required recovery baseline | Adds memory/disk/network consistency work without making effects atomic |

Official sources establish limitations rather than complete guarantees. The SDK mirror can drop failed batches and continue; store backed resume can leave the external mirror as its surviving transcript copy. Consequently commit needs an application durability barrier. Its conformance suite is useful but does not establish host loss recovery or our conditional recovery append contract. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage

Sessions preserve conversation separately from files; the same cwd/store identity matters across hosts. This supports independent session and workspace storage, not their atomic coupling. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions

EFS describes close to open consistency and Regional write durability on sync/close, with advisory locks. Treat these as a candidate fit, then test claim creation, directory durability and client behavior on the actual mount. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/features.html

Linux documents NFS O_EXCL support conditions and concurrent O_APPEND risks. Kubernetes access modes are not general mounted write protection. PostgreSQL synchronous commit protects local acknowledged WAL; asynchronous commit is unsuitable before dependent external actions. None of these facts establishes an unreachable executor has stopped.

Sources: https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html ; https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/ ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/wal-async-commit.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/explicit-locking.html ; https://docs.temporal.io/activity-execution

## Complete candidate and acceptance protocol

The Workflow owns run lineage, accepted checkpoint references, pending call identity, decision acceptance, recorded effect result and parked state. Segment/effect Activities remain ordinary Activities. Do not launch CLI or perform filesystem/provider IO from Workflow code. Use existing segment/effect queues without Worker affinity; all compatible Workers mount the same run paths. A lifecycle Activity integrates the existing supervisor with the chosen platform's authoritative termination facility, rather than building a second executor.

Proposed state sequence:

1. Starter supplies immutable lineage. Prepare validates package, policy, SDK/CLI/image digest, manifest and storage identity. Existing or missing unresolved claims cannot be converted to a fresh run.
2. Supervisor obtains serialized run admission and records sandbox instance/host identity. Prior owner termination must be verified, including descendants. A persistent ownership record prevents conflicting launches but its expiry is not termination proof.
3. Segment runs through SDK with effects deferred. On terminal pause, stop all session mutation and drain/contain the old process. Read exact session entries back from durable storage; validate original pending request and checkpoint chain. Any mirror_error, missing required entry or changed head refuses acceptance. Capture raw opaque entries, including metadata, rather than only the compacted visible conversation.
4. Persist an immutable candidate receipt containing lineage, checkpoint UUID, transcript digest, pending JSON digest, package/policy/engine and image fingerprints, volume identity/generation, workspace inventory digest and authoritative cleanup identity. A synchronous store transaction commits transcript sequence and receipt. Files are made durable and validated before creating the receipt. This is ordered validation, not a claimed distributed transaction between filesystem and database.
5. The Workflow accepts the receipt only after the Activity result is committed. A durable candidate receipt whose Activity completion was lost is an orphan, not accepted progress. Retried work reconciles with Workflow accepted state and cannot invent an effect. Mutable stale/unverified workspace parks rather than being implicitly restored. Before any accepted boundary is reused, validate both protected state and expected mutable file hashes.
6. Once accepted, Workflow schedules the external effect. For Bash create ordinal and key claims, durably sync their records/parent directory using qualified volume semantics before spawn. Partial dual claim creation, timeout, lost acknowledgement or existing claim parks. Claims stay protected and never imply completion.
7. After completion, persist the exact result and file postimages before delivery. A known durably recorded result may be returned without redispatch. An external action without a proven recorded result parks; a stdout log alone is not completion authority. Exact result adoption from an orphan completion record requires a separately tested reconciliation rule and immutable effect identity; otherwise conservatively park.
8. Replacement validates accepted receipt, authoritative old termination, volume and package consistency, then uses transactional append_if_unchanged through the existing original pending adapter. It must refuse changed UUID head, wrong result/input, unsupported children or mismatches before startup.

Do not invent whole workspace rollback as the default. Reads and deferred effects make accepted boundaries manageable, but supported tools may still change local engine metadata. Files altered after a accepted boundary without a durable effect result need explicit reconciliation or refusal. Capturing an inventory alone detects drift; it does not repair drift.

## State ownership, retention and restore

| State | Authority/storage and acknowledgement | Identity/consistency | Missing, stale or retention behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orchestration, decisions and accepted outcomes | Workflow history; committed Activity result/Update | Namespace, Workflow run, immutable lineage, decision/call IDs | Replay bounded references; retain through service policy; no history means no fabricated acceptance |
| Session trajectory | Transactional shared store; synchronous ordered append and read back | cwd project key, session UUID, entry UUID/type, checkpoint and digest | Missing accepted prefix parks; never fall back to fresh/local session; retention owner pending |
| Validated Skill and policy | Protected read only package on workspace plus immutable source digest | Package, exact Skill names, engine/policy/image digest | Mismatch refuses before claim; retain compatible package/Workers while runs recoverable |
| Workspace/artifacts | Durable POSIX volume; qualified sync/close/rename durability | Volume identity, lineage, generation, pre/post hash inventory | Unexpected files park; stale restore needs independent receipt comparison; no auto reprepare |
| Claims and uncertain outcomes | Protected volume directory, never effect writable; durable claim before spawn | Ordinal and key, lineage, original input/result | Missing expected claim parks; retain until namespace reset/replay retention ends; no unknown retention deletion |
| Execution ownership/termination | Protected serialized admission and platform supervisor receipts | Instance, host and lifecycle identity, admission epoch | Expired lease is not kill proof; unresolved old owner blocks replacement |
| Credentials/keys | Deployment secret system, only necessary runtime access | Run/deployment authorization and optional attestation | No storage of raw launch credentials in transcript/receipts; owner chooses encryption/rotation; unavailable keys park |

An accepted receipt held outside a restored filesystem can detect some rollback. Simultaneously rolling back its database and filesystem to a mutually consistent old state needs an independently retained accepted Workflow reference and recovery verification. Loss of all mutually independent authorities is outside supported recovery. Claim enumeration must be cross checked against accepted/uncertain effect identity; a matching volume generation alone is not enough.

## Capability and risk matrix

| Capability | Status | Risk if wrong / decisive requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serial original pending recovery and scoped permission controls | Locally demonstrated, bounded retained evidence | Different routes/versions may close callback stream; selected route only |
| Host local authoritative cleanup | Locally demonstrated | Does not prove disconnected remote host termination |
| Shared transactional conditional transcript append | Untested proposed integration | Two resumes append conflicting history; cross client CAS race test |
| SessionStore alone as strict durability | Unsupported | Mirror loses accepted entries; explicit barrier required |
| EFS close to open/Regional durability | Documented | Client cache/mount/permissions faults; actual volume proof |
| Claim atomicity and sync durability across hosts | Untested | Duplicate spawn or lost claim; contention/power loss tests |
| Workspace/checkpoint consistent restore | Untested | Recorded result with stale files; paired mismatch tests |
| Safe automatic takeover on partition using timeout | Unsupported | Old process continues and replacement duplicates execution |
| Effect isolation and confidential storage | Owner decision and untested | Bash edits protected records/reads credentials; adversarial OS tests |
| Arbitrary external exactly once execution | Unsupported | Success/completion recording gap; park or service specific proof |
| Accepted progress loss objective | Proposed: preserve every accepted boundary under chosen storage failure model | Unaccepted tokens can be recomputed; no numeric time target invented |
| Retention, security owner, deployment region/platform | Owner decision | Premature deletion or inappropriate risk acceptance |

## Failure traces and falsifiable proof plan

All proposed distributed tests are NOT executable now without a selected provisioned two host topology, storage adapter and fault harness. They use existing runner/supervisor as subjects; new instrumentation extends those fixtures. No live model is needed for the first storage/ownership tests: deterministic provider transport can expose unsafe continuation. Later real SDK/model acceptance needs separate scope and allowance. No prepared historical command may be reused.

Common future topology: two physically independent Linux hosts H1/H2, same qualified immutable image, SDK 0.2.162 / CLI 2.1.274 initially, shared chosen POSIX volume at identical cwd, transactional store on independent failure domain, existing Temporal proof service or explicitly selected service. Exact kernel, volume/NFS client options, database patch/replication policy and runtime versions must be pinned before execution. External oracle is an independent append only counter service recording effect identity and request receipt, not files on the killed host. Collect history, opaque transcript, accepted receipts, durable claims, workspace hashes, lifecycle receipts and oracle log in immutable captures.

| Test | Injection and expected result | Failure oracle and required evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A-T01 process/container/guest loss | Kill respectively SDK process, disposable container and guest before/after transcript acknowledgement. Before accepted receipt, restart/reconcile or park; after accepted commit, recover original pending result after termination proof | No fabricated checkpoint, exact accepted prefix, old instance dead, effect counter unchanged until accepted commit |
| A-T02 host/disk loss | Destroy H1 and its local disk after accepted commit. H2 mounts independent durable state and resumes; before result recording any started Bash parks | Exact receipt/session/files survive; original pending identity; one oracle request maximum; independent stop proof |
| A-T03 unreachable host | Block H1 control/service traffic while allowing oracle egress, cause Activity timeout, request replacement | H2 must refuse while H1 can still execute; no new CLI ownership or effect. Capture continued H1 oracle access and refusal. Merely waiting for lease expiry is a failed test |
| A-T04 volume/database partition | Interrupt volume sync and store append separately before acknowledgement and between file durability and receipt commit | No accepted boundary references missing data; zero effects after refused commit; record uncertain writes, recover by inspection rather than recreate |
| A-T05 rollback and partial restore | Restore workspace/claims older than accepted receipt, then store older than Workflow reference, then inconsistent paired restore | Admission refuses every missing/stale claim or hash; do not repeat Edit/Bash; matching generation does not falsely pass |
| A-T06 concurrent replacements | Barrier H1/H2 at admission and transcript conditional append; race same run/key/checkpoint | One accepted owner/append winner; loser prelaunch refusal; old winner cannot be replaced solely through expiry |
| A-T07 claim and effect gap | Kill before/after each ordinal/key claim sync, before/after spawn, before/after oracle success and result durability | Partial/existing claims park; success without result never redispatched; two requests for same identity fail test; no claim deletion |
| A-T08 recorded result recovery | Kill after durable known result and immediately before/after pending result append | Exact original result reused, CAS at correct head, no physical repeated effect; identical Boolean/number distinctions retained |
| A-T09 cancellation/descendants | Script detaches child that keeps making oracle calls; cancel/kill parent | Supervisor stops entire environment; no replacement until authoritative receipt; postreceipt child request fails proof |
| A-T10 version/package mismatch | Restore accepted run with changed SDK/CLI/image/package/policy or changed executor digest | Prelaunch/preclaim refusal; compatible lane succeeds only with explicit retained qualification |
| A-T11 answers at failure/handover | Accept same human answer through concurrent Updates while owner dies and Continue-As-New occurs | Exactly one recorded decision survives; original pending question and exact JSON answer recovered; deadline/dedup preserved; no signature bypass |
| A-T12 retention | Janitor sees idle, parked, terminated, reused Workflow ID and unknown namespace retention | Live/idle/parked state retained; wrong lineage does not delete; unresolved claims never deleted; closed files wait approved grace |

Each row requires a positive control and a guard weakening control. Remove claim validation, change accepted receipt hash, permit takeover on timeout or suppress termination checks in an isolated copy: the intended oracle must fail. A collection error is not a mutation kill. Tests additionally record restore duration and unaccepted recomputation; recovery time target is an owner decision. None of these tests proves every provider response, all filesystems, Byzantine host behavior or multi region disaster recovery.

Cleanup for each test: stop both old and replacement identities, terminate entire process tree/environment, obtain host/platform receipts from independent authority, verify no oracle requests after termination, retain ambiguous claims and captures. Cleanup refusal stops subsequent tests. Faults deleting storage must use disposable namespaces and backups with separate operator approval, never original raw evidence.

Smallest decisive experiment is A-T03 combined with A-T06 using deterministic transport: prove that an unreachable still executing original blocks replacement and that two proposed owners cannot both launch. It targets the architectural risk before spending on Claude. Requires provisioned two host control/egress separation, independent oracle and authority capable of confirming termination. No live model allowance needed, infrastructure costs require approval. If the product instead requires automatic partition failover, this experiment must establish enforcement that actually disables the original, not merely a lease claim.

## Integration work and open decisions

New code would be the transactional conditional SessionStore adapter, immutable durable receipt and workspace consistency validation, and platform lifecycle hooks in the existing supervisor. General workspace/effect executor, signed gateway, reset/Continue-As-New and janitor remain planned existing work. Preserve A-17/A-27/A-48/A-37/A-38/A-58/A-59 and propose evidence retirement at storage/ownership proof milestones, not discovery completion.

Owner must choose host failure scope, storage/platform availability, isolation/trust model and security role holder, transcript/reset retention, automatic partition availability versus safe parking, accepted progress loss/failure model and recovery time targets. Engineers can select among supported mechanisms once these requirements are explicit. No database, cloud account or confidential requirement has been silently selected.

Confidence is high that accepted boundary recovery without VM memory snapshots is feasible when termination and durable consistent state are available. Confidence in this particular distributed composition remains conditional until tests. Recommend it as the baseline competing candidate because it adds fewer correctness dependencies; preserve VM snapshot alternatives only if measured recovery time or other requirements demand them.
